question: Which of the following statements about legally blind individuals is true?

options.A: Most retain some form of residual vision or light perception
options.B: They cannot hear or speak normally compared to others
options.C: They experience total pitch darkness without any exceptions
options.D: Their condition can always be cured with minor surgery

explanation: Legal blindness is a definition for benefits and care, but very few people with this status see absolute blackness; most have usable light or shape awareness. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h3)

question: You just finished dressing a patient's wound with blood-stained gauze. Which bin should this gauze go into?

options.A: Black bin
options.B: Brown bin
options.C: Yellow bin
options.D: Clear bin

explanation: Well done! Blood-soaked materials are considered infectious waste, so they always go into the yellow bin or bag for safe, specialized treatment. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T5#GNS122_U5_T5_h2)

question: What kind of everyday triggers can set off painful muscle spasms in a baby with advanced tetanus?

options.A: Only deep surgical procedures
options.B: Administering routine oral medications
options.C: Feeding the infant warm breast milk
options.D: Minimal external stimuli like touch or noise

explanation: Spot on! Because the calming nerve signals are blocked, even a light touch, a sudden sound, or bright light can trigger violent, painful spasms. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T018#GNS226_U3_T018_h4)

question: Which type of vitamin can easily build up to toxic levels if taken in excess over time?

options.A: Water-soluble vitamins
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.C: Amino acid supplements
options.D: Plant-based minerals

explanation: Because fat-soluble vitamins get stored in body fat instead of being peed out quickly, taking too many of them over time can lead to a harmful buildup. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T013#GNS227_U7_T013_h5)

question: A patient complains of frequent hard stools and infrequent bowel movements. What is your best first piece of advice?

options.A: Eliminate all physical activity to rest the bowel
options.B: Stop eating all solid foods for forty-eight hours
options.C: Take strong prescription laxatives every morning
options.D: Increase daily water intake and eat more fiber-rich foods

explanation: Fluids and fiber are always the safest, most natural starting point to help a patient beat simple constipation. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T12#GNS213_U3_T12_h3)

question: What is needed to make community health schemes truly successful in Nigeria?

options.A: Government backing, transparent management, and public education
options.B: Making health insurance compulsory only for the wealthy
options.C: Complete elimination of primary health care centers
options.D: Relying solely on foreign donor grants forever

explanation: For long-term success, we need strong support from institutions, honest handling of funds, and well-informed citizens who understand the benefits. [learn more](GST322_U4_T4#GST322_U4_T4_h7)

question: Why is teaching patients how to avoid environmental hazards so important after an insect sting recovery?

options.A: It guarantees that insect populations will decrease around the home
options.B: It eliminates the patient's biological sensitivity to insect venom
options.C: It minimizes the chance of future exposure and repeat anaphylactic events
options.D: It replaces the need to carry emergency rescue medications

explanation: Prevention is key! Simple steps like wearing protective clothes keep patients out of harm's way so they don't experience another scary reaction. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h8)

question: A junior nurse makes a minor error while trying a new wound care dressing. What response shows true psychological safety?

options.A: Publicly reprimanding her during the next shift handover meeting
options.B: Banning her from ever performing wound care on the unit again
options.C: Treating the error as a learning opportunity and reviewing the steps together
options.D: Issuing a formal written warning and placing it in her permanent file

explanation: A supportive unit uses mistakes as stepping stones to teach and mentor, keeping patient care safe and morale high. [learn more](GST319_U2_T5#GST319_U2_T5_h6)

question: A patient with long-term malabsorption shows up with easy bruising and bleeding gums. Which vitamin deficiency is the likely culprit?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Vitamin B1
options.C: Vitamin K
options.D: Vitamin A

explanation: Spot on! Fat-soluble vitamins like Vitamin K need healthy fat absorption to enter the body. Without it, clotting factors drop, leading to easy bruising and bleeding. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T7#GNS121_U1_T7_h7)

question: Why is high reliability so important for our nursing research tools?

options.A: It proves the researchers spent enough money on equipment
options.B: It ensures study results are free from random measurement errors
options.C: It guarantees that patients will recover faster on the ward
options.D: It stops patients from dropping out of clinical trials early

explanation: Reliable tools cut out the guesswork and random noise. When we use them, we can trust our data reflects what's truly happening on the ward! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h1)

question: Which male reproductive gland adds the most fluid volume to semen?

options.A: Seminal vesicles
options.B: Prostate gland
options.C: Testicular interstitium
options.D: Bulbourethral glands

explanation: Spot on! The seminal vesicles are generous contributors, providing about 60% of semen fluid along with sugary fructose to give the sperm energy. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T1#GNS311_U1_T1_h4)

question: How does a functional drug classification differ from a therapeutic one?

options.A: It focuses strictly on the financial cost of the medication
options.B: It describes how the drug works at a cellular or physiological level
options.C: It dictates the preferred route of administration for the nurse
options.D: It lists only the herbal ingredients found in traditional remedies

explanation: While therapeutic class tells you the disease treated, functional class explains the exact body process or cellular mechanism the drug alters. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T4#GNS125_U2_T4_h2)

question: What is a parallax error when reading a scale, and how do you prevent it?

options.A: An error caused by the patient wearing heavy rubber shoes
options.B: An inaccurate reading caused by looking at the scale from an angle instead of straight at eye level
options.C: A mechanical failure caused by sliding the heavy counterweight too fast
options.D: A false measurement resulting from an unlevel floor surface

explanation: Looking at a scale from above or below skews the numbers. Always read the measurement directly at eye level to get it right! [learn more](GNS225_U2_T8#GNS225_U2_T8_h5)

question: What is a direct way to check the quality of youth-friendly services from the clients' own viewpoint?

options.A: Counting the number of chairs in the parking lot
options.B: Gathering feedback through exit interviews and suggestion boxes
options.C: Reading national textbooks on adult medicine
options.D: Checking the personal financial records of the nursing staff

explanation: Spot on! Asking the young clients directly via suggestion boxes or quick chats lets you know what's working and what needs fixing. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T48#GNS214_U1_T48_h8)

question: What is the medical term for painful menstrual cramps caused by trapped blood behind scar tissue?

options.A: Dysmenorrhea
options.B: Amenorrhea
options.C: Menorrhagia
options.D: Polymenorrhea

explanation: You got it! Dysmenorrhea means painful periods—and the pain becomes severe when scar tissue blocks menstrual blood from flowing out normally. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T4#GNS225_U6_T4_h3)

question: How are findings usually shown in a quantitative (numbers-based) results section?

options.A: Using emotional poetry and personal journal entries
options.B: Using text, statistical values, tables, and graphs
options.C: Using unformatted raw audio files from interviews
options.D: Using long narrative stories and fictional metaphors

explanation: Tables, charts, and clear numbers make it easy for readers to see what the data is telling us at a glance. [learn more](GNS224_U3_T3#GNS224_U3_T3_h5)

question: A mother brings her toddler to the clinic with 10 episodes of watery diarrhea today. Which assessment finding requires immediate nursing action?

options.A: Mild fussiness when the mother tries to feed him
options.B: Sunken fontanelle and no wet diapers for six hours
options.C: Mild low-grade fever of 37.8 degrees Celsius
options.D: Loose stool containing small pieces of undigested food

explanation: A sunken fontanelle and lack of wet diapers indicate dangerous dehydration and reduced kidney perfusion, requiring urgent fluid resuscitation. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h3)

question: Why do we say out-of-pocket spending is a rough deal for patients?

options.A: It forces families to pay directly at the point of care, leading to financial hardship
options.B: It requires too much paperwork for hospital administrators
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for government hospitals
options.D: It increases the overall supply of essential medicines too quickly

explanation: Paying cash right at the hospital door can wipe out a family's savings overnight when a sudden sickness hits. That's why health insurance is so important! [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h1)

question: Which of the following does NOT help build a strong research culture?

options.A: Discouraging nurses from reading studies done by other healthcare professions
options.B: Creating mentorship programs between senior and junior staff
options.C: Establishing local grants to fund small nursing projects
options.D: Providing protected time during work hours for research activities

explanation: Healthcare is team-based! Shutting out studies from other professions hurts teamwork and slows down evidence-based practice. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h6)

question: Administrative nursing informatics is primarily used for which of the following tasks?

options.A: Administering intravenous medications directly to patients
options.B: Managing staffing schedules, budgets, and operational metrics
options.C: Designing interactive smartphone apps for general public use
options.D: Conducting laboratory experiments on cellular disease models

explanation: Nurse leaders use administrative tools to oversee hospital operations, staffing levels, and financial or quality metrics. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T2#GNS113_U1_T2_h3)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier that keeps young girls out of school in vulnerable communities?

options.A: High costs of school fees and uniform supplies
options.B: Guaranteed free university placement for all female students
options.C: Cultural preference for educating boys over girls
options.D: Long and unsafe travel distances to the nearest classroom

explanation: Spot on! Free university placement isn't a barrier. Instead, high costs, long distances, and gender bias are the real obstacles keeping girls out of classrooms. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T12#GNS312_U1_T12_h7)

question: What do the ciliary muscles do when you switch from looking at a distant wall to reading a book close to your face?

options.A: They pull the iris wide open
options.B: They contract to make the lens thicker
options.C: They relax to make the lens thinner
options.D: They push the cornea outward

explanation: For close-up reading, your ciliary muscles tighten up, letting the lens get nice and round to focus clearly. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS211_U4_T6#GNS211_U4_T6_h3)

question: What is a top nursing priority right after a patient has joint replacement surgery?

options.A: Restricting all fluid intake to prevent joint swelling
options.B: Monitoring for signs of deep vein thrombosis and encouraging early movement
options.C: Encouraging complete bedrest for at least two weeks
options.D: Removing the surgical dressings immediately to check the bone

explanation: Well done! Getting the patient moving early and checking for blood clots are vital steps to keep them safe after surgery. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h7)

question: What is the medical term for the exaggerated inward curve of the lower back seen in pregnancy?

options.A: Cervical subluxation
options.B: Compensatory lumbar lordosis
options.C: Thoracic scoliosis
options.D: Lateral kyphosis

explanation: Lordosis is just the natural inward curve of the lower back. During pregnancy, it becomes more pronounced (exaggerated) to help balance out the heavy bump. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h3)

question: What movement decreases the angle between two bones, like bending your elbow?

options.A: Extension
options.B: Flexion
options.C: Abduction
options.D: Pronation

explanation: You nailed it! Flexion is bending a limb to decrease the angle at a joint—like bringing your hand closer to your shoulder. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T5#GNS121_U3_T5_h5)

question: Why must local Rapid Response Centers connect with national disaster frameworks?

options.A: To eliminate the need for local emergency supplies and equipment
options.B: To ensure that hospitals never have to report patient statistics
options.C: To transfer all administrative responsibilities away from local community leaders
options.D: To ensure seamless sharing of personnel, funding, and resources across jurisdictions

explanation: When a local disaster gets too big to handle alone, connecting with national networks makes it easy to call in extra hands and supplies. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why are hip and spine fractures very common in elderly patients with weakened bones?

options.A: These bones are made entirely of cartilage instead of bone.
options.B: These regions contain high amounts of fragile cancellous bone.
options.C: These bones are never protected by muscle tissue.
options.D: These areas never undergo normal bone remodeling.

explanation: Areas like the hip, wrist, and spine are packed with delicate cancellous (spongy) bone. When someone develops osteoporosis, these spongy areas lose their strength first, making them prime spots for fractures. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T3#GNS121_U3_T3_h5)

question: When checking if an unresponsive patient is breathing normally, what is the maximum time a nurse should spend on this?

options.A: One minute
options.B: Thirty seconds
options.C: Ten seconds
options.D: Two minutes

explanation: Nice and quick! We check for breathing and a pulse at the same time, but we never want to waste precious seconds—keep it under 10 seconds so compressions aren't delayed. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h3)

question: What is a vital safety step when nursing a patient with Wernicke encephalopathy?

options.A: Setting up fall precautions because of poor coordination
options.B: Encouraging heavy gym workouts to build leg strength
options.C: Restricting all fluids to stop brain swelling
options.D: Keeping the room pitch black all day

explanation: Spot on! Because these patients struggle with balance (ataxia), keeping them safe from nasty falls is a top nursing priority. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T7#GNS222_U4_T7_h6)

question: How does health promotion differ from basic disease treatment?

options.A: It relies entirely on expensive surgical interventions
options.B: It focuses on environmental conditions and empowerment rather than just fixing illness
options.C: It is handled exclusively by doctors in private clinics
options.D: It only applies to children and elderly populations

explanation: While disease treatment steps in after sickness occurs, health promotion looks at the bigger social and living conditions that keep people well in the first place. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: A researcher wants to record the exact physical behaviors of nurses during a sterile dressing change. Which instrument should they use?

options.A: Observational checklist
options.B: Structured interview guide
options.C: Patient satisfaction survey
options.D: Biographical questionnaire

explanation: Observational checklists are ideal for watching and recording specific actions as they happen in real time. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T21#GNS224_U1_T21_h3)

question: How do you properly check the function of cranial nerve XI (the spinal accessory nerve) in an adult?

options.A: By checking if the patient can stick out their tongue straight
options.B: By shining a bright light into both of the patient's eyes
options.C: By asking the patient to shrug their shoulders against resistance
options.D: By testing the patient's ability to hear a whispered voice

explanation: Just place your hands on their shoulders and ask them to shrug against your push. That tests cranial nerve XI easily! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T4#GNS222_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is one of the biggest challenges facing local disaster agencies in Nigeria?

options.A: Chronic underfunding and a lack of modern rescue equipment
options.B: An excessive surplus of advanced medical helicopters
options.C: Strict adherence to international space agency guidelines
options.D: Too many trained volunteers refusing to work

explanation: That's right. Many local agencies struggle simply because tight budgets make it hard to buy modern gear and keep emergency vehicles running. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T8#GNS315_U1_T8_h8)

question: A stable patient needs daily IV antibiotics and physical therapy after a severe foot ulcer infection. Where should they be admitted?

options.A: An intensive care unit
options.B: A subacute care facility
options.C: An outpatient primary clinic
options.D: A long-term custodial home

explanation: Exactly! Needing daily skilled nursing (like IV medications) plus active therapy fits the exact description of subacute care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h2)

question: How does the stress-relaxation response help an organ like your urinary bladder?

options.A: It forces the organ to empty immediately when it reaches half capacity
options.B: It prevents the muscle cells from ever fatiguing during hard work
options.C: It generates rapid pumping movements to mix internal contents
options.D: It allows the organ to stretch to hold more fluid without a sharp pressure spike

explanation: This clever response lets your bladder gradually accommodate more fluid as it fills up, preventing sudden uncomfortable pressure spikes. Nursing clinicals will make this super clear too! [learn more](GNS121_U3_T11#GNS121_U3_T11_h6)

question: When is an employer usually NOT held liable for a nurse's action?

options.A: When the nurse engages in a major personal detour from work duties
options.B: When the nurse follows a hospital protocol that contains a minor flaw
options.C: When the nurse makes a standard medication calculation error on the ward
options.D: When the nurse takes a short authorized break inside the hospital building

explanation: If you leave your post to go handle a major personal errand far away, you've stepped outside your job description, and the hospital is off the hook for what happens. [learn more](GST321_U10_T6#GST321_U10_T6_h3)

question: How does severe anaemia affect the uterus while a woman is in active labor?

options.A: It makes the cervix open twice as fast.
options.B: It blocks blood flow through the umbilical cord.
options.C: It causes the water bag to break immediately.
options.D: It deprives the hardworking womb muscle of oxygen, leading to poor contractions.

explanation: Just like any muscle working hard at the gym, the uterus needs good oxygen to push effectively. Anaemia makes that tough! [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h2)

question: Why is diet therapy such an important part of your daily nursing duties?

options.A: Nurses must personally cook all meals served in the hospital ward
options.B: Nurses are responsible for monitoring patient tolerance and supporting the prescribed nutrition plan
options.C: Dietary plans replace the need for physical assessments
options.D: Doctors never check what patients are eating

explanation: Since you spend the most time with patients, you are in the best position to see if they are enjoying their food and how well their body is handling it! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T22#GNS214_U1_T22_h1)

question: Why must wrapped instrument trays be loaded loosely inside a steam sterilizer?

options.A: To allow steam to circulate freely around every package
options.B: To stop the external indicator tape from melting off
options.C: To prevent the heavy metal trays from breaking the door
options.D: To make unloading faster for the nursing assistant

explanation: If the packs are crammed too tightly together, the steam can't reach every surface, leaving pockets where germs can survive. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T7#GNS122_U2_T7_h5)

question: Unlike in wealthy nations where older women are mostly affected, what is the typical age group for breast cancer in Nigeria?

options.A: Younger women between thirty-five and fifty years
options.B: Elderly women over the age of eighty years
options.C: Adolescent girls during puberty
options.D: Infants with congenital genetic mutations

explanation: You'll often see breast cancer diagnosed in younger women here in Nigeria, unlike the older postmenopausal pattern seen in high-income countries. Keep this in mind during community postings! [learn more](GNS313_U3_T9#GNS313_U3_T9_h1)

question: What do we call it when cancer cells break away and spread to other parts of the body through the blood or lymph system?

options.A: Apoptosis
options.B: Mitosis
options.C: Metastasis
options.D: Hyperplasia

explanation: You've got this! Metastasis is simply the word for when cancer travels from its original spot to start new tumors elsewhere. Great job! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h1)

question: Why must standing order protocols be reviewed and updated regularly?

options.A: Older protocols automatically expire and turn invisible after thirty days
options.B: Medical guidelines and disease treatment recommendations change over time
options.C: Government printing presses need new contracts every single month
options.D: Patients prefer reading newly printed paper booklets during visits

explanation: Clinical practice evolves as new evidence emerges, so standing orders must be updated to reflect current, safe medical standards. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h9)

question: Which of these is an example of 'chemoprophylaxis' in public health?

options.A: Administering the BCG vaccine to a newborn baby in the clinic
options.B: Isolating a patient with cholera in a treatment tent
options.C: Giving antimalarial medication to pregnant women to prevent malaria illness
options.D: Educating mothers on exclusive breastfeeding for six months

explanation: Chemoprophylaxis simply means using protective drugs to stop an infection before it can make a vulnerable person sick. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T16#GNS313_U1_T16_h5)

question: When does hospice care typically begin for a patient with a terminal illness?

options.A: At the exact moment of diagnosis
options.B: When the patient has about six months or less to live
options.C: Only after the patient loses consciousness
options.D: When family members request discharge home

explanation: Hospice care is designed for individuals who have a prognosis of six months or less if the terminal illness runs its typical course. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T12#GNS321_U4_T12_h1)

question: When should a nurse refer a postpartum mother to a specialized family planning clinic?

options.A: When a new mother refuses to hold her baby after a normal delivery
options.B: When routine postpartum lochia transitions from red to yellow-white
options.C: When the infant develops mild neonatal jaundice in the first week
options.D: When a client has a complex medical history requiring expert evaluation

explanation: Mums with underlying health conditions like severe high blood pressure need expert guidance to pick the safest contraceptive method. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T023#GNS226_U3_T023_h4)

question: What is the term for the surgical procedure to cut scar tissue during childbirth in women with infibulation?

options.A: Curettage
options.B: Defibulation
options.C: Clitoroplasty
options.D: Hysterectomy

explanation: Defibulation is the surgical opening of the fused labia to allow for normal childbirth and examination. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T6#GNS312_U1_T6_h4)

question: How do thyroid hormones affect a person's Basal Metabolic Rate?

options.A: They slow down heart rate to conserve oxygen inside the vital organs
options.B: They regulate water balance to prevent rapid shifts in body weight
options.C: They stimulate fat cells to store extra energy during periods of rest
options.D: They act as the main accelerator for cellular energy use across the body

explanation: Your thyroid gland is like the engine's spark plug. Its hormones control how fast your cells turn nutrients into energy, setting your overall metabolic pace. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T9#GNS121_U1_T9_h2)

question: An autistic patient gets very upset when you shift their routine by just ten minutes. What core feature does this reaction show?

options.A: An intentional attempt to disrupt the ward
options.B: A sign of sudden memory loss
options.C: A rigid adherence to routines and resistance to change
options.D: A lack of basic physical sensation

explanation: It's completely normal for them to feel unsettled here. Predictability brings comfort, so unexpected changes to routines can cause real anxiety. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T5#GNS324_U4_T5_h2)

question: What is most important for a tele-nurse trying to check a patient's skin rash over a video call?

options.A: Adequate lighting in the patient's room
options.B: The presence of background music
options.C: The brand of the patient's television
options.D: High room temperature

explanation: Good lighting is key! Without it, the camera won't show the true color and texture of the skin. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T6#GNS113_U3_T6_h5)

question: Why is daily foot care and inspection so crucial for patients with diabetes?

options.A: Daily observation increases blood circulation to the toes
options.B: Sweat buildup guarantees the rapid development of gangrene
options.C: Nerve damage can prevent them from feeling minor cuts or blisters
options.D: Skin color changes indicate the exact blood sugar level

explanation: Diabetes can cause nerve damage (neuropathy) in the feet, meaning minor sores can go unnoticed and turn into major wounds if not checked daily. Essential nursing wisdom! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T17#GNS324_U4_T17_h6)

question: What is the main job of the transport media in a collection tube?

options.A: To keep microorganisms alive without letting them multiply
options.B: To change the color of the sample for easy identification
options.C: To chemically digest human cells surrounding the bacteria
options.D: To kill all normal flora present on the swab

explanation: Transport media acts like a safe holding zone. It keeps the germs alive for the lab without letting them multiply out of control. [learn more](GST114_U5_T1#GST114_U5_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary role of nurses regarding disability policy frameworks?

options.A: To penalize families who miss therapy appointments
options.B: To advocate for policy enforcement and connect families with support resources
options.C: To write and pass new national constitutions
options.D: To collect taxes for hospital construction

explanation: Nurses act as patient advocates, helping families access rights and benefits guaranteed under existing laws. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h8)

question: What is the most common type of prospective observational study used in healthcare research?

options.A: Cross-sectional survey
options.B: Cohort study
options.C: Historical review
options.D: Case report

explanation: Cohort studies follow groups of participants over time to observe the development of specific health outcomes. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T15#GNS224_U1_T15_h2)

question: Why is it important for healthcare workers to understand the basic economics of food pricing?

options.A: It prevents nurses from ever having to worry about patient dietary budgets
options.B: It allows clinics to set direct retail prices for medications and supplies
options.C: It explains how economic shifts directly impact household nutrition and health outcomes
options.D: It qualifies nurses to manage local agricultural farms and crop yields

explanation: Understanding financial pressures helps clinicians recognize why patients might struggle to afford healthy diets. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T026#GNS227_U2_T026_h1)

question: A patient with diabetes has a fasting blood sugar of 55 mg/dL and is shaky and confused. What is the most likely cause of these symptoms?

options.A: Kidney failure causing a backup of metabolic waste
options.B: A normal reaction to an overnight fasting period
options.C: Dehydration from drinking too much plain water
options.D: Brain glucose deprivation from low blood sugar

explanation: When blood sugar drops too low, the brain lacks energy, causing neurological symptoms like confusion and shaking. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T12#GNS221_U2_T12_h7)

question: Which treatment method is required for pathological waste and body parts?

options.A: Microwaving
options.B: Incineration
options.C: Municipal composting
options.D: Standard laundering

explanation: That's right! High-temperature burning (incineration) is the safest way to completely destroy anatomical and pathological waste. [learn more](GST114_U6_T5#GST114_U6_T5_h6)

question: What is the main goal of therapeutic drug monitoring?

options.A: To confirm that the medication is producing the desired clinical effect
options.B: To test if the patient is secretly selling their prescription
options.C: To ensure the pharmacy department bills the patient correctly
options.D: To prove that the physician chose the cheapest available brand

explanation: We monitor to make sure the drug is actually helping the patient heal and not causing trouble. Spot on! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T9#GNS125_U1_T9_h5)

question: What should you do if you are unsure about a drug dosage calculation?

options.A: Give half the amount to be safe and wait for complaints
options.B: Have a second nurse independently calculate and verify the dose
options.C: Call the hospital security team to supervise the injection
options.D: Guess the amount based on the patient's physical size

explanation: Two brains are better than one! Getting an independent double-check from a colleague is a gold standard for catching math errors before they reach the patient. [learn more](GNS125_U4_T5#GNS125_U4_T5_h4)

question: What is the main job of the Theatre Sterile Supply Unit (TSSU)?

options.A: Disposing of hazardous biological waste from wards
options.B: Manufacturing single-use surgical equipment
options.C: Processing, sterilizing, and distributing medical instruments
options.D: Conducting pre-surgery patient assessments

explanation: You've got this! The TSSU is the heartbeat behind every clean surgery. Its main job is to safely clean, sterilize, and hand out surgical tools so patients stay infection-free. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h1)

question: A patient is receiving an anti-bleeding infusion. What is the most critical thing for the nurse to keep watching for?

options.A: Testing urine sugar levels after every meal

question: Why can handing out donated infant formula be dangerous in poorly sanitized displacement camps?

question: A client 4 weeks post-vasectomy asks if he can stop using condoms since he feels great. What is your best advice?

question: How does false community rumor about vaccine safety affect overall immunization success?

options.A: It forces manufacturing companies to recall all expired vaccine batches

options.C: It causes healthcare workers to administer incorrect dosages

question: Which disease is linked to water sources contaminated with sewage?

question: Why should you avoid fancy 3D effects when making pie charts?

question: Which resting position is best for improving circulation and comfort during pregnancy?

question: What is a major benefit of connecting a visually impaired patient with a peer support group?

options.C: Sharing practical coping strategies and reducing isolation
options.D: Replacing the need for professional nursing home care

question: You are wrapping up an admission chat with a new patient. Which action belongs to the termination phase?

options.C: Asking open-ended questions about childhood medical history

question: Why should a nurse know the difference between normal aging and an actual disease?

question: What does it mean for a nursing research project to show 'originality'?

options.A: Adding fresh insights or applying concepts in a new setting

options.C: Writing a research paper without using any past references
options.D: Copying successful studies from foreign countries word-for-word

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard nursing responsibility during a routine patient discharge?

options.A: Documenting the exact time and manner of the patient's departure

question: Why can't you rely solely on looking at a vaccine to know if heat has ruined it?

options.A: Heat damage does not change the physical appearance of the liquid

question: Why is relying heavily on staff overtime a poor long-term way to save money?

options.A: Overtime is usually paid at a higher premium rate and leads to staff burnout
options.B: Overtime payments are never recorded in the unit operational budget
options.C: Working extra hours causes nurses to forget all their clinical training

question: What was the traditional view of a man's primary role in family health?

options.A: Clinic scheduler
options.B: Primary caregiver

explanation: Traditionally, men were viewed mainly as providers of money rather than active participants in daily health care and clinic visits. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h1)

question: Which level of healthcare prevention includes traditional rehabilitation activities?

options.A: Secondary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Primary prevention
options.D: Tertiary prevention

explanation: Tertiary prevention is all about managing existing long-term issues, preventing complications, and getting the patient to their highest possible function. [learn more](GNS123_U6_T1#GNS123_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is a macronutrient that our bodies need in large amounts?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Minerals
options.C: Water-soluble enzymes
options.D: Vitamins

explanation: Carbs, proteins, and fats are your macronutrients—the heavy lifters our bodies need in big quantities every day! [learn more](GNS227_U4_T005#GNS227_U4_T005_h2)

question: Why are structured tools like SBAR so helpful for community health teams?

options.A: Government regulations require every home visit to be recorded on video
options.B: Printed records are completely banned in rural clinics
options.C: Team members work in different locations and need clear, quick updates

explanation: Spot on! Since community staff operate out in the field, quick and clear updates keep everyone on the same page. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h4)

question: What is the safest way to bend down and pick up a heavy item off the floor?

options.A: Bend at your knees and hips while keeping your back straight
options.B: Twist your upper body sideways as you reach down
options.C: Arch your back backward before lifting upward
options.D: Bend forward only at your waist with stiff knees

question: Which lifestyle advice is most important for a nurse to emphasize during patient education for sickle cell anaemia?

options.A: Restrict fluid intake in the evening to prevent frequent nighttime urination
options.B: Maintain consistent daily hydration and avoid extreme temperature changes
options.C: Wear tight, supportive clothing to keep the peripheral blood vessels compressed
options.D: Engage in intense competitive sports to build strong cardiovascular endurance

question: According to Maslow's hierarchy, which level of needs forms the base of the pyramid?

options.A: Self-actualization
options.B: Safety and security
options.C: Love and belonging
options.D: Physiological needs

explanation: Physiological needs like air, water, and food sit at the very bottom of the pyramid because they are essential for immediate survival. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h2)

question: What is the main downside when a nurse suffers from 'under-delegation' (refusing to delegate tasks)?

options.A: Excessive free time for nursing assistants on the ward

options.C: Immediate legal prosecution for negligence by the hospital board

explanation: Trying to do everything yourself on a shift is a fast track to burnout. Trust your team and share the load! [learn more](GST321_U1_T15#GST321_U1_T15_h5)

question: What does an "unmet need" for family planning mean?

options.A: Using birth control despite wanting to get pregnant
options.B: Being unable to find a pediatrician in a rural clinic
options.C: Experiencing side effects from modern oral pills
options.D: Wanting to avoid pregnancy but using no contraception

question: What should you do if a patient calls reporting sudden chest pain and severe shortness of breath?

options.A: Ask them to send a text message if the pain gets worse tomorrow

options.C: Instruct them to immediately seek emergency medical care or transport
options.D: Advise them to drink warm water and sleep for an hour

question: When does tertiary prevention come into play during the course of an illness?

options.A: Before any risk factors are present in the community
options.B: During routine health promotion and wellness talks
options.C: After disease and complications have already occurred
options.D: When conducting mass screening tests for healthy adults

question: What is the main purpose of a low-calorie diet?

options.D: Creating an energy deficit for weight loss

question: Which of these is NOT a core principle of a Drug Revolving Fund?

options.A: Maintaining strict financial accountability and transparency

options.D: Ensuring constant availability of essential medicines

question: A patient died with an IV line in place and a coroner's post-mortem is requested. What should the nurse do with the line?

options.A: Hide the lines under the bedsheets
options.B: Remove all lines immediately to clean the skin
options.C: Leave all lines and tubes in place
options.D: Cut the tubing short and tape it down

question: Why are there spaces between the bars in a standard bar chart?

options.A: To show that the categories are separate and distinct

question: Why do different organizational cultures, such as military versus humanitarian groups, cause friction in a response?

question: Why should a 38-year-old client who gets migraines with aura avoid combined oral contraceptives?

options.C: It significantly increases her risk of having a stroke

question: Why must you NOT apply suction while pushing the catheter down into the tracheostomy tube?

question: When a patient has tummy pain, asking what makes the pain better or worse helps you figure out what?

question: Why is it important for a nurse to tell normal sadness apart from clinical depression during an assessment?

question: Which blood marker is commonly measured to help screen for prostate disorders?

question: If a patient misses work for weeks due to a hospital admission, how is their lost salary classified?

question: What is the simple difference between responsibility and accountability?

question: Which of these is a POSITIVE, 100% sure sign of pregnancy?

question: Why do clinical nurses need to team up with environmental health officers?

question: How does insoluble fiber specifically help your tummy and bowels?

question: Why does the Essential Drug Programme focus heavily on generic medicines instead of brand names?

options.B: Brand-name drugs are scientifically proven to be unsafe for public use

question: What is the main purpose of the thick mucus layer inside your stomach?

question: What is a common challenge that QA committees face in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.C: Having way too many medical doctors and nurses in every ward
options.D: Severe staff shortages and heavy workloads leading to fatigue

question: Why is waste segregation at the point of generation considered so important in healthcare facilities?

options.A: It reduces the physical weight of general rubbish bins

options.C: It ensures hazardous infectious waste is treated correctly before final disposal
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for cleaning hospital floors

question: What is the main trigger that causes blood vessels in the newborn lungs to relax and open?

question: What do home ovulation predictor kits mainly test for in urine?

options.C: Basal body temperature

question: What is an 'outlier' on a scatter diagram?

question: When is it most appropriate to give a patient an antitussive (cough suppressant)?

options.C: For clearing thick, green mucus from the lungs
options.D: For lowering a high fever during the flu

question: How can severe stress or trauma in childhood affect a person later in life?

options.C: It can alter brain development and prime the nervous system to overreact to future stress.

question: Which type of exercise is crucial during late recovery to retrain joint awareness and prevent future sprains?

question: What is the primary goal of palliative care in a geriatric setting?

options.D: Speeding up the dying process to save facility resources

question: What is the main purpose of a formal grievance procedure in a hospital?

options.C: To resolve staff complaints fairly without fear of victimization
options.D: To bypass national labour laws during salary negotiations

question: Why should hospitals offer counseling and support to nurses involved in errors?

question: Why is intersectoral collaboration important in primary health care?

options.B: It ensures that hospitals make a higher financial profit

question: Which of these is a duty of nursing management rather than leadership?

question: A nurse is caring for a patient with end-stage kidney disease. Which sign is most directly linked to the kidneys losing their hormone-making job?

question: How is the adult ear canal structured from outside to inside?

question: What is the main job of a research question in a nursing study?

question: In what kind of situation would an intracardiac injection most likely be considered?

question: What is it called when a baby's head is simply too big to fit through the mother's pelvis?

options.D: Placenta previa

question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of kwashiorkor?

options.B: Rapid overgrowth of the long bones
options.C: Generalized pitting edema and skin changes
options.D: An extremely high fever with sudden seizures

question: Which term describes a complete loss of feeling or touch sensation in a part of the body?

options.A: Hypesthesia

options.C: Analgesia
options.D: Anesthesia

explanation: Anesthesia means total absence of feeling. You'll hear this word in surgery too, where patients are given drugs to block all sensation! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T20#GNS222_U3_T20_h4)

question: What primary tool do auditors use to collect data during a nursing audit?

options.A: Surgical scalpels and sterile dressing forceps

options.D: Structured checklists and patient case notes

question: What is a very common reason new mothers delay their first bowel movement after delivery?

options.B: Severe dehydration that dries out all body fluids

question: Which blood vessel carries oxygen-rich blood from the placenta to the baby?

options.A: Inferior vena cava
options.B: Ductus arteriosus

options.D: Umbilical artery

question: What is one of the biggest advantages of using the team nursing model?

options.B: Cost-effective use of mixed staff cadres working together
options.C: Complete elimination of any need for supervision
options.D: Patients never have to interact with nursing assistants

explanation: Spot on! Team nursing lets hospitals blend different skill levels efficiently, making patient care well-organized and resourceful. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T4#GNS123_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which chemical messenger in the brain ramps up electrical activity during a seizure?

options.A: Acetylcholine

question: During which week of enteric fever are dangerous complications like intestinal bleeding or tears most likely to happen?

options.A: Eighth week

options.D: First week

question: Why should a nurse check lab results before confirming neurasthenia?

options.A: Medical conditions like anemia or infections share similar symptoms of fatigue

options.C: Hospital policy requires a blood test for every single mental health visit

question: When measuring the length of a 10-month-old infant, what should you do with their legs?

options.C: Wrap both ankles tightly together with a soft bandage

question: What is a major social reason why communities practice food taboos?

options.A: Preventing all forms of infectious diseases
options.B: Maintaining social order and group solidarity
options.C: Encouraging international food trade
options.D: Lowering the cost of agricultural production

explanation: Think of food rules as a way communities bond. Sharing the same dietary dos and don'ts brings people together and keeps their shared traditions strong. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T016#GNS227_U2_T016_h2)

question: How do environmental health challenges generally differ between urban and rural settings?

options.A: Rural areas are overcrowded while urban areas have vast open farmlands
options.B: Urban areas are completely free from any form of environmental hazards
options.C: Urban areas have more industrial pollution while rural areas face agricultural risks
options.D: Both settings experience identical levels of traffic congestion and smog

explanation: You got it! Cities deal with traffic and factories, while villages face challenges like farming chemicals or lack of clean water sources. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T2#GNS225_U1_T2_h5)

question: What does the balance column on a stock card represent?

options.A: The number of expired items thrown away that month

question: What shape does a perfectly balanced, symmetrical data distribution make?

options.A: A flat horizontal line
options.B: A bell-shaped curve

explanation: Nice one! A normal distribution makes a lovely bell shape where the mean, median, and mode all sit right in the center together. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T2#GNS217_U4_T2_h5)

question: What is the main job of the innermost layer of the gut (the mucosa)?

options.A: Secreting mucus and absorbing nutrients
options.B: Providing a tough outer protective cover
options.C: Supplying blood vessels to the muscle layer
options.D: Pushing food forward through peristalsis

explanation: You got this! The mucosa is the innermost lining of your digestive tract, and its main work is to secrete protective mucus and absorb all the good nutrients from your food. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T011#GNS227_U1_T011_h1)

question: According to the WHO moments for hand hygiene, when is Moment 5?

options.A: Immediately before making physical contact with the patient
options.B: After accidentally touching spilled blood on the floor
options.C: After touching inanimate objects in the patient's immediate surroundings
options.D: Before performing a sterile dressing change

question: Which factor actually helps lower a woman's chances of getting epithelial ovarian cancer?

options.A: A woman who used oral contraceptive pills for over five years
options.B: A woman with a strong family history of breast cancer
options.C: A woman who underwent early menarche and late menopause
options.D: A nulliparous woman of advanced maternal age

question: What is a primary sign of compassion fatigue in a healthcare worker?

options.A: A sudden increase in physical body weight and strength
options.B: Excessive excitement and eagerness for every shift
options.C: Extraordinary patience with difficult administrative tasks
options.D: Emotional numbness and exhaustion from constant caregiving

explanation: Compassion fatigue happens when exposure to continuous suffering drains a nurse's emotional reserves, causing burnout and detachment. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h7)

question: Why is it risky for a patient to stop taking their antibiotics early just because they feel better?

options.A: The kidneys will stop producing urine due to sudden chemical toxicity
options.B: The toughest bacteria can survive, multiply, and cause a stronger, drug-resistant infection
options.C: The patient will permanently lose their normal bowel flora
options.D: The body will develop an immediate allergy to that specific drug class

explanation: Stopping early leaves behind the strongest germs. They bounce back stronger and won't respond to the same medicine next time! [learn more](GNS223_U8_T2#GNS223_U8_T2_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of evaluating a newly introduced nursing practice?

options.A: To reduce the total number of patients admitted to the hospital
options.B: To increase the monthly salary of the lead ward nurse
options.C: To check if the change actually improved patient outcomes
options.D: To punish staff who made mistakes during the trial

explanation: Exactly! Evaluation is simply asking: 'Did our new idea actually help the patient get better?' It keeps our care goal-focused. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T3#GNS224_U4_T3_h6)

question: When is incidence density preferred over regular cumulative incidence?

options.A: When every single patient is followed for the exact same number of years
options.B: When the researcher wants to measure total existing chronic cases
options.C: When the population size remains completely frozen with zero movement
options.D: When participants enter a study at different times or drop out early

explanation: Real life is messy—people join studies late or drop out. Incidence density handles these rolling timelines like a champ. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T86#GNS214_U1_T86_h5)

question: A patient with a history of epilepsy comes to the clinic reporting frequent seizures after spending a week studying all night for exams. Which trigger is most likely responsible?

options.A: Genetic mutation
options.B: Flashing lights
options.C: Sleep deprivation
options.D: Cerebral infection

explanation: Severe lack of rest significantly lowers the brain's seizure threshold and is a very common trigger for acute attacks. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T16#GNS222_U3_T16_h4)

question: A patient is having a sudden panic attack on the ward. What is the best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Telling the patient to stop worrying about nothing
options.B: Guiding the patient through slow, controlled breathing exercises
options.C: Administering a high-dose herbal supplement immediately
options.D: Leaving the patient alone in a quiet room to sleep

explanation: Deep, slow breathing triggers the body's calming system, helping to physically slow down anxiety and panic right away. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T3#GNS314_U4_T3_h3)

question: Which chemical messenger relaxes blood vessels in the penis to start an erection?

options.A: Nitric oxide
options.B: Acetylcholine
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Dopamine

explanation: When arousal happens, nerve endings release nitric oxide. This is the green light that relaxes the smooth muscles so blood can rush in. [learn more](GNS121_U4_T1#GNS121_U4_T1_h4)

question: Why do children get medication doses calculated by body weight instead of a standard adult dose?

options.A: Children metabolize all drugs faster than adult patients
options.B: Children have developing organ systems and varying body sizes
options.C: Liquid medications always require weight-based measurements
options.D: Standard adult doses are illegal to give to anyone under age twelve

explanation: Kids aren't just tiny adults! Because their little bodies and metabolic organs are still growing, weight-based dosing keeps them safe from accidental overdoses. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T4#GNS125_U3_T4_h7)

question: A tele-nurse sees that a heart failure patient's daily weight readings are steadily climbing. What should the nurse do next?

options.A: Contact the patient to assess for worsening fluid overload symptoms
options.B: Ignore the data until the patient's next scheduled annual checkup
options.C: Advise the patient to stop taking all prescribed medications immediately
options.D: Delete the readings because home devices are always inaccurate

question: Why do we treat active tuberculosis with multiple drugs instead of just one antibiotic?

options.A: It makes the treatment course last much longer.
options.B: It eliminates the need for any nutritional support.
options.C: It lowers the risk of common stomach upsets.
options.D: It prevents the bacteria from easily developing drug resistance.

explanation: Hitting the TB bacteria with a combination of strong drugs makes it nearly impossible for the germs to mutate and outsmart the treatment. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T5#GNS214_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is the primary job of cytotoxic T cells?

options.A: To form the physical skin barrier against outside bacteria
options.B: To slow down the immune response once an infection clears
options.C: To produce massive quantities of free-floating antibodies
options.D: To destroy virus-infected or abnormal body cells directly

question: An older adult patient admitted with dizziness tries to get out of bed unassisted to use the bathroom. What is the best immediate preventive action?

options.A: Tie the patient's hands securely to the bed railings
options.B: Turn off the room lights so the patient stays in bed to sleep
options.C: Scold the patient for trying to walk without asking first

question: Why do nurses and doctors pay very close attention when a lab report mentions dysplasia?

options.C: It means the cells have permanently shrunk due to prolonged starvation

question: Where should a nurse document a medication error and the subsequent patient assessment?

question: What is the main goal of 'task-shifting' in mental health care?

question: Why is a structured handover important when transferring a patient to the postnatal ward?

question: Which care delivery system assigns specific tasks, like giving out meds or doing wound dressings, to different nurses?

question: What does indirect calorimetry measure to calculate energy use?

options.C: Oxygen consumption and carbon dioxide production
options.D: Electrical resistance of skin tissue

question: Which hormone helps your body hold onto water when you are dehydrated?

options.C: Insulin

question: What is the most important advice for a patient who just received IV contrast dye?

question: Why is it smart to involve local community leaders when planning health teaching strategies?

question: Which vaccines does a newborn baby routinely receive right at birth here in Nigeria?

question: Which patient is the best candidate for a soft diet?

question: Which major protein in the blood plasma binds heavily to many circulating medications?

question: Where does the growing uterus usually push the stomach during pregnancy?

question: Why do teenage girls need more daily iron in their diet than younger children do?

question: Oops! A scrubbed nurse accidentally drops their hands below waist level before putting on a gown. What should they do?

question: Which of the following is NOT a common barrier to healthy eating for vulnerable psychiatric patients?

question: Which blood-borne infection has the highest statistical risk of transmission after a single accidental needle-stick?

question: A nurse is getting the delivery room ready for an expected birth. What should be checked first?

options.B: Staging extra visitor chairs around the bed for family members

question: Why is GNP an important concept for nurses to understand?

options.C: It measures the exact recovery rate of patients admitted to emergency wards

question: You see an infected villager walking toward the local drinking pond to soothe a burning leg blister. What should you do first?

question: What is the main feature of a non-experimental research design?

question: How does a 'just culture' handle a mistake made by a healthcare worker?

options.C: It assumes that nurses never make unintentional mistakes

question: At what age might a nurse suspect a motor issue if an infant consistently prefers using only one hand?

question: What happens during 'data cleaning' after data collection?

question: Which criterion is commonly used when setting priorities among several community health problems?

options.B: The personal preference of the visiting medical doctor

question: How can severe physical or emotional stress lead to spaced-out periods (oligomenorrhoea)?

question: You are alone with a patient having a severe drug reaction. After stopping the IV, what should you do next?

question: Your patient has a severe head injury and declining consciousness, but your clinic has no surgeon. What is your next best step?

question: Why is getting the partner's approval emphasized so heavily during family planning counseling?

question: Which of the following items is classified specifically as sharps waste?

question: What administrative problem frequently disrupts the availability of essential medicines in clinics?
